title.narrative: Stöd till UNICEF Liberia land program
Support to UNICEF Liberia country programme

description.narrative: The objectives of the UNICEF Country Programmme, and specifically, the Child Protection Thematic Area from 2020-2024 have not changed substantively from the previous program period. Rather, after an extensive consultative review process of the previous country programme, UNICEF has focused its programming, and as a result, has tightened its intended objectives. They are as follows: Output 5.1: By 2024, Strengthened political commitment, accountability and national capacity of social, justice and education and health sectors in Liberia to legislate, plan, and budget for scaling up interventions that prevent and respond to violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect and enhance access to child protection and birth registration Output 5.2: By 2024, accessible and quality birth registration and child protection (prevention and response) services are in place and delivered by qualified statutory and non statutory service providers in most disadvantaged localities in Liberia Output 5.3 By 2024, children, families and communities have increased capacities in the most disadvantaged localities to promote practices that protect them through addressing gender inequitable norms, values and practices that are detrimental to boys, girls including adolescents/young people Output 5.4 By 2024, an improved knowledge base/baseline that inform programming and advocacy initiatives to increase access to birth certificates and to prevent and protect children and women from violence, abuse and exploitation

UNICEF har inkommit med en ansökan om finansiering till Sveriges ambassad i Liberia om 8 MSEK för ett smidigt genomförande av organisationens landprogram i Liberia. Det övergripande målet med programmet är att möta behoven för utveckling och skydd bland landets barn och unga.
Ambassadens stöd är öronmärkt till programmets komponent som rör barns skydd, vars mål är att bidra till att bygga och stärka barns trygghetssystem genom kapacitetsutveckling på nationell och subnationell nivå. Detta kommer främst att göras genom uppbyggandet av gemenskapsbaserade trygghetssystem för barn, främjandet av allmän födelseregistrering, stärkandet av säkerhetsnät , lagar och policys för barns skydd, samt främjandet av ungdomars och ungas egenmakt med syftet att öka deras deltagande i besults- och fredsprocesser.
Den totala budgeten för landprogrammets komponent för barns skydd är USD 2 600 000, varav ambassadens bidrag utgör SEK 8 000 000 vilket motsvarar ca USD 881 000.
UNICEF:s landkontor i Liberia kommer att genomföra programmet i samarbete med departementen som i första hand är ansvariga för barns rättigheter och skydd i Liberia (Jämställdhets-, Hälso- och Justitiedepartementet). Även interreligiösa råd, gemenskapsbaserade organisationer och andra icke-statliga aktörer förväntas spela en nyckelroll.

UNICEF has applied to the Embassy for funding of 8,000,000 SEK to help address funding gap that has undermined smooth implementation of its overall country programme. The UNICEF country programme is aimed at addressing the development and social protection needs of children and young people.
The Embassy’s support will be earmarked for the child protection component, with the objective of contributing to building and strengthening children’s social protection systems through capacity building at both national and county levels. The key activities under the programme are building community based child protection systems, promoting universal birth registration, strengthening safety nets and child protection laws and policies, as well as empowering adolescents and young people to participate in decision making and peace processes.
The total budget for this component is USD 2.6M, of which the Embassy’s contribution will be the amount of approximately USD 881,000 (Eight Million Swedish Kronor).
UNICEF’s Country Office in Liberia will implement the programme in partnership with the Ministries of Gender, Health, and Justice that have got oversight responsibilities over child rights and protection in Liberia. Inter-religious councils, community based organizations and other non-governmental organizations will play a key role as well.

title.narrative: Agreement between Sweden and UNICEF - Amendment 1

description.narrative:
UNICEF is working closely with the Liberian government, particularly the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) providing financial and technical support. This has resulted in strengthened capacity of the social service workforce, more coordinated interventions providing unified services across health, education and protection, and improved systems for better child protection outcomes.
Examples of results achieved in 2025 include:
Strengthening Child Protection Systems in Liberia
- UNICEF advanced key reforms to professionalize and expand the social service workforce.
- UNICEF and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) strengthened the frontline child protection systems and evidence-based case management by addressing critical workforce shortages through a partnership with accredited universities.
- The MoGCSP, the Ministry of Education (MoE), and the Ministry of Health (MoH) worked in close coordination to bridge two major national initiatives, the Support a Child, Save the Future project and the Back to My Classroom Campaign. By linking these programmes, the government moved away from isolated services to a unified approach that offers protection, education, and healthcare simultaneously.
- The national care reform for children moved forward as the MoGCSP officially endorsed the revised foster care guidelines, minimum standards, and training manuals, setting clear quality benchmarks for safe, familybased alternative care.
- The deployment of 25 trained social workers to communities affected by mpox ensured families had immediate access to psychosocial support and protection from GBV, while updating national response plans and proposals to include child protection alongside Health and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) sectors.
Advancing National Efforts to End Violence Against Children
- Liberia advanced the operationalization of its national pledges to Ending Violence Against Children (EVAC) by 2030, following commitments made at the first Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence against Children in Bogota.
- a National Steering Committee and a Technical Working Group were constituted to guide the development of a national strategy that translates Liberias EVAC pledges into actionable priorities, roles, and timelines.
- UNICEF supported the GEnder Based Violence (GBV) Division of the MoGCSP to advocate for fee waivers for survivors of GBV, including sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), at public health facilities such as One-Stop Centers and referral hospitals. This coordinated approach has removed a major hurdle to care, ensuring that survivors receive the timely, high-quality, and supportive services they need.
- At the national level, UNICEF also supported efforts to address VAC rooted in harmful traditional practices by forming a multi-stakeholder technical committee to lead the way on legal reform. The committee is developing a roadmap which together with its concept note is a major step toward creating permanent laws that protect children.
Strengthening the Juvenile Justice System
- Liberias specialized child justice system remains operational and is being strengthened through dedicated courts, police units, and training programmes designed to safeguard childrens rights and ensure child-sensitive procedures. During the reporting period, UNICEF supported the OWECC to advance transitional justice for children, reinforcing accountability and victim-centred approaches.
- Collaborating with the Ministry of Justice and key rule-of-law institutions, UNICEF prioritized diversion as a primary alternative to detention for children in conflict with the law, particularly those accused of minor offences.
Improving Birth Registration, Civil Registration, Vital Statistics and Identity Systems
- UNICEF strengthened the countrys Civil Registration, Vital Statistics, and Identity Management (CRVSID) ecosystem by partnering with the MoH, the National Identification Registry (NIR) and other partners to drive policy and service delivery reforms.
- UNICEF partnered with the NIR and MoH to pilot national identity registration for children under six, integrating birth registration, issuing a unique identifier at birth, and verifying immunization status. The pilot reached 5,082 children under six, demonstrating a practical model for early identity assignment and cross sectoral service linkage from birth.
- At the service delivery level, UNICEF and MoH continued to accelerate universal birth registration through the implementation of three key accelerators: decentralization, digitalization, and interoperability. Financial, logistical, and technical support were provided, enabling the full digitization and decentralization of 58 birth registration centres nationwide, including 42 centres in health facilities, one at a district health office, and 15 at the county service centres. As a result, 98 percent of districts across Liberia now provide free and universal birth registration services.
Enhancing Child Participation, Advocacy & Adolescent Empowerment
- During the reporting period, UNICEF strengthened child participation, advocacy, and adolescent empowerment through a series of strategic initiatives, including key commemorative events. Notably, in partnership with government ministries and child protection organizations, UNICEF commemorated the 2025 Day of the African Child (DAC) and World Day Against Child Labour. As part of this effort, over 500 children from all 15 counties participated in a national advocacy event held under the theme Investing in our Future: Prioritizing Child Rights and Ending Child Labour through Budget and Action.
- UNICEF further strengthened adolescent and child participation by expanding structured platforms that amplify young peoples voices and promote their leadership in national and regional decision-making spaces. Through strategic partnerships, adolescents, particularly girls, actively participated in high-level engagement fora, including Liberias National Adolescent Girls Conference and the West and Central Africa Girls Summit in Dakar, Senegal.
- Translating participation into leadership and protective outcomes, adolescent girls in Gbarpolu and Grand Gedeh counties emerged as change agents in their respective communities. Through peer educator networks and girls Buddy Clubs, adolescents are leading violence-prevention initiatives, promoting school retention, strengthening life skills, and challenging harmful gender and social norms that increase risks of violence, exploitation, and exclusion.
